cell_status.description: `superseded` is NEW in this type and is the corpus's characteristic failure: a source that 301s to a live replacement is NOT `unreachable` — the fetch succeeded — and a 404 from a discontinued programme is not a transient outage. `forbidden-by-terms` will never fire here: no registry row PROHIBITS automated access. Several rows do address it and three carry an affirmative grant, so read the row — addressed-and-permitted is a different state from unaddressed. An enum value that cannot fire is not a defect, but its silence would otherwise read as a coverage gap.

queries.description: EVERY query run for this pair, verbatim AS RUN. A paraphrase cannot be re-run, and a coverage record that cannot be re-run proves nothing.

status.description: What happened to this SOURCE. One cell per active source — not per mechanism, since a cell has no mechanism field and two cells for one source would collide on `source_id`. `reached` means content was retrieved and counted. `superseded` means the fetch SUCCEEDED at a new location — a redirect to a live replacement is not a failure, and recording it as `unreachable` hides that the corpus is moving under the survey. `unreachable` asserts the different thing: it was attempted and no content came back.

returned.description: How many ITEMS this cell found, under the frame `count_frame` states. Required when status is `reached`. The unit is the angle's: contribution points for an enumeration angle, matching passages for a policy angle — which is exactly why `count_frame` is required alongside it, since two competent agents counting the same page under different frames both report honestly and differ. NULL — never 0 — for any other status: a zero meaning 'we could not look' is the failure this survey exists to prevent.

count_frame.description: What `returned` counted and how it was derived, stated so a reader can re-derive it: "h2 headings over raw HTML", "distinct sentences matching the recorded regexes, deduplicated". Required in spirit whenever `returned` is above 0 — a count without its frame is not re-derivable, and this type's corpus yields six defensible counts for one page.

kept.description: How many distinct CANDIDATE ROWS this cell carried into `candidates` — the same meaning the sibling types give it. Not items: an enumeration angle admits 38 contribution points and emits ONE row carrying `enumeration.count: 38`, so kept is 1. It must EQUAL the number of candidates citing this source. kept = 0 where `returned` is above zero owes an `unadmitted` entry or a note saying why nothing survived; where returned is also 0 there was nothing to survive and nothing is owed. NULL, never 0, for any non-`reached` status.

cause.description: Required for every non-`reached` status, with observable evidence: an HTTP status, a redirect target, an error string.

variant_read.description: Which representation of this source you actually read, when it publishes more than one — an `llms.txt`, a `.md` variant, the rendered HTML. The variant is part of the record: two agents reading different variants of one URL can honestly report different counts.

fallback_used.description: The registry id of the fallback actually used, prefixed with which level it came from: `angle:<id>` for the angle's declared fallback, `row:<id>` for the source row's own. They differ — `cws-policies` falls back to `chrome-ext` at row level and `chromium-ext-group` at angle level — and one bare string cannot say which was walked.

platform_slug.description: MUST exist in the wave-0 map. An angle that mints its own slug breaks the dedupe.

locator.description: For an enumeration candidate, WHERE the enumerable set lives — a count without its location cannot be re-derived.

retrieved_at.description: When we fetched it. Ours, on our own authority.

as_of.description: When the FACT became true. NULL when the content states none — never defaulted to the fetch date, which is the difference between saying we do not know and lying.

source_claimed_modified_at.description: What the page says about ITSELF. A BELIEF, not a fact: RFC 9110 defines this as what the origin server believes, and this corpus contains a page footer-dated 2012 that documents a 2023 format.

source_claim_provenance.description: Where the self-claimed date came from. `absent` is recorded explicitly rather than left null-by-omission.

evidence_quote.description: The load-bearing sentence, VERBATIM from the source at `locator`. Not a paraphrase: three conditions judge the claim against this text, and a paraphrase is the author's reading rather than the document's words.

claim.description: What the DOCUMENT says, in your words — never what the platform does. `evidence_quote` is the warrant for this sentence; if the two do not match, the quote governs.

finding.description: An ABSENCE that is itself evidence: "the guidelines state no commission rate anywhere". Recorded here rather than left as an empty field, because a hole reads as an oversight and this reads as a fact about the corpus.

announced_on.description: a4 only. When the change was announced. Separate from `enforced_on` because the INTERVAL is the finding, and a prose sentence saying "about four years" cannot be divided by anything.

enforced_on.description: a4 only. When it took effect.

enumeration.description: A count is meaningless without its FRAME. Six defensible counts came out of one enumerable set on one day, differing only by which question they answered.

branch.description: Which conditional branch of the artifact was counted, where it has one.

reconciled_by.description: The SECOND independent derivation. Not belt-and-braces: an extraction of a machine-readable catalog once returned a well-formed row that did not exist, caught only by mechanical re-derivation.

schema_version.description: The version THIS schema validates. A const, not a floor: `minimum: 1` accepted a v2 artifact and silently judged it against the v1 rules, which is the one failure a version field exists to prevent.

outcome.description: An unrun angle owes NO coverage cells — writing empty ones would manufacture zeros that look like searches.

coverage.description: One cell per ACTIVE SOURCE — the sources the angle declares, its declared fallback, and any row-level fallback actually walked. A source with no cell is an unexplained gap, not a zero. Not per mechanism: the map's `mechanisms` build the QUERIES a cell records, they do not multiply the cells.

retrieval_summary.description: Deliberately duplicates the cell statuses: it is the record a reviewer reconciles the cells against, and a discrepancy is the signal that a failure was laundered into a zero.

bound.description: The per-angle limit, whether it bound, and the ordering it truncated by. The flag is `hit`, matching every sibling type; `bound` was this type's own spelling for the same concept and diverged from all three.

cap.description: The REGISTRY's cap for this angle. A run may neither raise its own ceiling nor quietly lower it.

hit.description: True when the cap actually truncated. False is the stronger claim: every admissible candidate is present.

ordering.description: The rule the truncation selected by, stated so a reader can re-apply it. An outcome restated ("the most relevant first") cannot be re-applied, and so cannot show what was dropped.

ordering_deviation.description: Set when you did NOT apply the declared ordering, with the reason. Strict application can drop the only quantified or only dated evidence in a corpus; a declared ordering a producer may never depart from is a worse rule than one that requires the departure to be recorded here rather than buried in `dropped_note`.

dropped_note.description: What fell out, when `hit` is true. Without it the ordering is the ONLY evidence a truncation leaves, which is what makes a vacuous ordering unreviewable rather than merely untidy.
